claims.exact_statement: For same source support, generator/SDE unconfoundability follows if there exists at least one source y whose positive drift-covariance cones are disjoint; requiring disjointness at every source is incorrect. The published Theorem 3.3(2) states the latter universal condition, while Theorem 5.15 and its proof establish confoundability iff every source intersection is nonempty.
assumptions: Finite mass-action reaction networks on the same species set
Strictly positive rate constants
Faul-Hoessly-Xia local Langevin/SDE uniqueness and generator-law hypotheses
claims.status: source-reported published statement plus internally reconstructed correction and exact counterexample; no external author correction checked
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a correction of a published quantifier statement derived from the paper's own confoundability theorem and proof; no novelty or author intent claim.
claims.costs: No experimental or computational cost; exact symbolic argument.
claims.falsifier: Find positive rates for the explicit 0->A,A->0 versus 0->2A,A->0 networks yielding identical drift and covariance on an open interval; coefficient equations show this would require alpha=2 alpha'=4 alpha'.
claims.next_gate: Independent expert verification and check for an author-posted correction/erratum.

claims.exact_statement: For a fixed linear sensor H and known controlled full initial concentration x, equality of the observed local drift and covariance response fields on an open set is equivalent to equality of sourcewise projected coefficient vectors. Positive rate vectors matching those fields exist iff all projected source cones intersect; hence one empty projected intersection rules out local-response confounding.
assumptions: Finite networks with mass-action monomials and positive rates
Known linear readout H
Known full state at each controlled initial intervention, though only HX is measured as output
Response notion is conditional local first and second characteristics, not Markov generator or full partial-output path law
claims.status: internally reconstructed conditional theorem; proof included; external correctness and priority unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: The source paper explicitly leaves partial observation as future work; related deterministic few-species identifiability exists for restricted network classes. This projection argument is short and priority is unverified.
claims.costs: Requires candidate reaction graphs, H, controlled known full initial concentrations, source-cone LP checks, and local drift/covariance measurements.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample where all projected source coefficients match on an open set but the stated local response fields differ, or where one projected source cone is disjoint yet positive-rate response fields match on an open set.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review; extend or delimit against arbitrary partial-output path-law equivalence and unknown hidden initial concentrations.

claims.exact_statement: Given m distinct source monomials and an admissible open concentration box, m rational setpoints can be selected with invertible monomial evaluation matrix W. Pointwise local-response errors at most eta yield source coefficient error at most sqrt(m)||W^{-1}||_2 eta. If source coefficient sets under supplied positive compact rate boxes are separated by delta, nearest-set classification is correct when sqrt(m)||W^{-1}||_2 eta < delta/2.
assumptions: Same projected local-response setting as claim projected-source-cone-local-response
Admissible concentration set contains a nonempty open box
Finite distinct source exponent set known from candidate networks
Rates constrained to compact intervals bounded away from zero for a positive uniform margin
Local response estimates have a certified deterministic error bound
claims.status: internally proved algorithmic consequence; no empirical estimator or finite-window error bound implemented
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses polynomial interpolation and compact-set separation; no claim that generic finite-design or optimal experimental-design literature is exhausted.
claims.costs: m interventions and local-response estimates; exact rank search and dense O(m^3) matrix solve; error amplification ||W^{-1}|| and margin delta; sensor-panel search may cost 2^n LP checks.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the coefficient error bound under exact W, or a bounded-rate pair with disjoint projected cones but zero distance between their compact coefficient sets.
claims.next_gate: Use cycle-2 stopped-increment bounds with a well-conditioned intervention matrix, then validate real reset/readout/interlock assumptions.

claims.exact_statement: For N={B->A+B,A->0} versus N'={B->2A+B,A->0}, observing A alone while setting a=1 and intervening at b=1,2 isolates source-B local characteristics (k,k) versus (2 lambda,4 lambda), which cannot coincide for positive rates. If all rates are in [1,2], the two source coefficient sets have Euclidean gap 2, and pointwise response error eta<1/2 suffices for the two-setting contrast classifier. The matched ODE baseline can be confounded by k=2 lambda and mu=mu'.
assumptions: Langevin approximation is valid over short observation windows
B is a controlled concentration and is unchanged by the catalytic reactions
Only A is output-measured; full initial setpoint is known
Rates are positive; robust margin uses dimensionless rate box [1,2]
Estimated local drift/variance pair has per-setting Euclidean error below 1/2
claims.status: exact symbolic model calculation; experimental execution and nature-level validation absent
claims.novelty_boundary: Illustrative application of the conditional projected-cone theorem; not an empirical biological finding or priority claim.
claims.costs: Finite instantiation: 2 setpoints, 6,000,000 independent starts per point, h=1e-4, 12,000,000 resets total, at least 24,000,000 scalar endpoint reads, continuous A-channel stop monitoring, A reset and B setpoint error at most 1e-6, gain error at most 1e-6, and per-read additive residual at most 5e-7. These are assumed bounds, not measured hardware facts.
claims.falsifier: Validated local-response estimates within eta<1/2 that place both candidate source-B coefficients in overlapping sets, contrary to exact separation; or failure of the Langevin response prediction in the physical system.
claims.next_gate: Compare the finite variance-slope test against a robust stopped-CIR likelihood and ODE-only baseline after validating instrument/monitor bounds.

claims.exact_statement: For a C2 diffusion on compact K stopped/held at first exit, with bounded drift/diffusion, independent repeated starts whose reset errors are at most rho, calibrated linear sensor gain error epsilon_H, and arbitrary adversarial endpoint-increment readout residual norm at most nu, the estimators (Rh)^-1 sum Y_r and (Rh)^-1 sum Y_rY_r^T satisfy the displayed high-probability bounds beta_a+s_a and beta_Q+s_Q. The beta terms explicitly include reset and setpoint uncertainty, sensor-gain error, finite-window generator bias, stop-exit probability, drift-square/cross terms, and readout residual; s terms are coordinatewise Bernstein bounds. The data analysis uses endpoint H increments only; an invariant set or implementable stop interlock is a separate operating assumption/cost.
assumptions: C2 coefficients on a neighborhood of K; uniform bounds B,S and generator/Lipschitz bounds on K and over any setpoint uncertainty box
All replicate reset choices are fixed before the runs or randomized independently of path data; fresh diffusion increments are independent conditional on the fixed reset list
Stopped process is held at the first exit and the stopping/censoring rule can actually be implemented
Known nominal linear H and operator calibration bound epsilon_H; endpoint residual differences are deterministically bounded by nu, with no zero-mean or independence assumption
Finite-window local response is the conditional mean/covariance of the stated diffusion model, not an empirical claim about a chemical system
claims.status: internally derived conditional finite-sample theorem with proof sketch and explicit constants; not externally reviewed or experimentally validated
claims.novelty_boundary: Generic concentration, stopped-Ito bias, and moment estimation are standard tools. The proposed contribution is only the explicit combination for the projected Langevin source-response interface; priority is unverified, and moment-based error-guaranteed inference for stochastic reaction networks with unobserved species already exists for the CME model.
claims.costs: R independent resets per setpoint; two endpoint readings per run plus safety monitoring/interlock cost; setpoint/reset precision rho/rho_u; gain calibration epsilon_H; endpoint residual nu; known bounded coefficients and stop probability; matrix dimension and Bernstein sample size. No experimental cost or data were acquired.
claims.falsifier: A verified counterexample to any of the stated stopped-process bias/concentration inequalities under their assumptions, or an admissible model/reset/noise instance violating the displayed bound.
claims.next_gate: Independent stochastic-analysis proof review and measurement of real reset/readout/interlock bounds; compare to a same-data model-aware likelihood.

claims.exact_statement: For N={B->A+B at rate k, A->0 at rate mu} and Nprime={B->2A+B at rate lambda, A->0 at rate muprime}, with only A read, controlled B setpoints 1 and 2, all four rates in [1,2], h=1e-4, K_A=[0.5,2.5], A reset/setpoint uncertainties 1e-6, gain error 1e-6, endpoint residual at most 5e-7 each, and the stated B,S,Lipschitz/generator bounds, the stopped-increment variance-slope threshold at 3 using R=6,000,000 starts per setpoint has error probability at most 0.05 uniformly over each network rate box. The true nominal variance slope is in [1,2] for N and [4,8] for Nprime; the finite bound gives slope estimation error below 0.8395.
assumptions: The observed one-dimensional A Langevin diffusion is valid over each short window and the B control is constant
The A-channel interlock stops/holds the process on K_A; monitor threshold uncertainty is included in the stated reset/location bound
Fresh independent starts, rate boxes supplied, two fixed setpoints, bounded sensor calibration/readout/reset/setpoint errors as stated
All constants have the concentration/time units used by the displayed SDE; no natural-system validation
claims.status: explicit internally calculated finite-data discrimination theorem for a conditional model; no experiment or simulation performed
claims.novelty_boundary: Illustrative application of the sourcewise projected-characteristic result. A specialized shifted-CIR likelihood uses the same endpoint increments and has an exact transition law; no statistical advantage or novelty priority is claimed.
claims.costs: 12,000,000 trajectories total, h=1e-4 each; at least 24,000,000 scalar endpoint readings, continuous A-channel safety monitoring/interlock, 12,000,000 resets, 1e-6 reset/setpoint/gain envelope and 5e-7 per-endpoint residual envelope. No hardware or physical data costs measured.
claims.falsifier: Within the model and stated boxes, finding an allowed rate tuple with q(2)-q(1) outside [1,2] or [4,8], or violating the computed beta/statistical bounds. In a real system, failure to reproduce the contrast with validated noise bounds falsifies the model-to-data bridge.
claims.next_gate: Run a matched finite-data benchmark against robust/exact stopped-CIR likelihood and an ODE-only baseline; first validate instrument and monitor bounds.

claims.exact_statement: At fixed B=b, the A-only Langevin SDE in N becomes a CIR diffusion after Z=A+kb/mu, and in Nprime after Zprime=A+4 lambda b/muprime. Thus an exact scaled noncentral-chi-square endpoint transition density is available in the un-stopped model. It is a same-channel/same-setpoint model-informed likelihood control; with bounded adversarial readout it must be robustified over compatible latent increments, and with stopping it must use the stopped transition kernel or censoring atom.
assumptions: Fixed b during each replicate
The candidate SDE equations and rates are correct
Known-readout likelihood claims assume a known stochastic readout law; bounded adversarial noise is treated as an interval nuisance
The exact un-stopped CIR kernel approximates the stopped experiment only up to the explicitly bounded exit probability
claims.status: internal algebraic reduction; no likelihood optimizer or power comparison run
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a model-specific existing statistical control, not a new CIR theorem. It blocks claims that the sourcewise variance statistic is more efficient than equally informed model-based inference; minimax superiority was not evaluated.
claims.costs: Likelihood evaluation/profile over the same rate boxes and per-run reset/setpoint nuisance bounds; for stopped trajectories solve/evaluate the one-dimensional stopped transition kernel; no computation time was benchmarked.
claims.falsifier: An error in the shift-to-CIR algebra or transition parameter mapping; a direct comparison may show the robust likelihood impractical, but no such comparison is currently available.
claims.next_gate: Derive/implement the stopped-CIR robust likelihood and compare worst-case finite-sample error and compute against the moment rule.
